paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The line chart titled “Errors (COPA)” displays the empirical generalization error of fine-tuned adapters on the COPA benchmark as a function of adapter rank, with error bars indicating variability. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is logarithmically spaced and marked at 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the hidden dimension size of the adapters. The y-axis, labeled “Errors (COPA),” is linearly scaled from 0.0 to 0.6 in increments of 0.3, quantifying the generalization error. A single black solid line connects four green circular markers, each with vertical error bars. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.22; at rank 16, it drops slightly to about 0.18; at rank 64, it rises sharply to 0.45; and at rank 256, it remains nearly constant at approximately 0.46. The trend shows a local minimum at rank 16, followed by a substantial increase in error as rank grows beyond 64.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors (labeled “Errors (COPA)”) for fine-tuned adapters using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B, evaluated across different adapter ranks (4, 16, 64, and 256). The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is on a linear scale ranging from 4 to 256, with tick marks at each specified rank value. The y-axis, labeled “Errors (COPA),” is also linear, spanning from 0.0 to 0.6, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.3. A single black solid line connects four green circular markers, each representing the mean error at a given rank, with vertical error bars indicating variability. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.15; it decreases slightly to about 0.12 at rank 16, then rises sharply to 0.45 at rank 64, and remains nearly constant at 0.45 at rank 256. The error bars are largest at rank 256 (spanning roughly 0.3 to 0.55) and smallest at rank 16, suggesting higher uncertainty for larger adapters.
